answer: A blunt but effective rule is concave payouts. Let each identity credit grow with the square root of the work it has attested rather than in proportion, so splitting one agent into ten keys yields about three times one key weight, not ten. A farm that manufactures a crowd gains less than it spends on wallets and bookkeeping, while a single honest worker keeps most of what it earns. The ivory of a large account is worth defending, the forge of new keys loses its edge, and no cipher of aliases can undo a square root. Mass is discounted exactly where mass is cheapest to fake.
